title: The Pastel Brutalist
logline: The Ontario mall where Robin Sparkles played her biggest show is being demolished, and its farewell gala wants its most famous performer back. Robin refuses until she learns she was the committee's third choice, while Ted's crusade to save the world's only example of Pastel Brutalism shrinks from a mall to an atrium to a dais to a single pink tile.
coldOpen: Kids, a shopping mall in Ontario once decided to throw itself a funeral. It wanted one last song. And it wanted your Aunt Robin to sing it.

couch.line: In Canada, everything gets a funeral. A few years later they held one for the penny.

guests.name: Darlene Pelletier
guests.role: general manager of the Glenhaven Galleria in Ontario since 1979, who is also its farewell committee, the township heritage board and the demolition foreman's wife; delivers devastating news with a bright smile and calls everyone 'dear'

scenes.summary: Darlene Pelletier drives nine hours to hand-deliver an invitation: the Glenhaven Galleria is being demolished and wants its most famous performer back for the farewell. Robin refuses; Barney is desperate; Ted discovers the mall is the only example of Pastel Brutalism and declares war on its demolition. A flashback shows Robin Sparkles' show was huge, and that she pinky-swore to come back. Darlene lets slip Robin is only 'one of' their famous performers.

beats.line: Woman at the bar. Mustard cardigan. She's been staring at you for twenty minutes.
Process server?
Worse. Canadian. Look how politely she's staring.
Robin Scherbatsky! Darlene Pelletier, Glenhaven Galleria. I drove nine hours, dear. Our stamp budget went to the fountain.
Never heard of it. Never been to Ontario. Not convinced it exists.
You signed my forearm in 1990, dear. I didn't wash it until Easter.
You've been in the same room as Robin Sparkles. What did she smell like?
Hairspray and ambition, dear.
We're being demolished on the twenty-first. So we're throwing ourselves a little farewell.
Light refreshments. Heavy machinery.
beats.title: The Glenhaven Goodbye
lines: Saturday the 20th, 7 p.m. Light refreshments. Heavy machinery.
Featuring the return of our most famous performer!

beats.line: No.
Oh, lovely. Is that a Canadian no? Where you show up anyway with a casserole?
It's an American no. I've been practicing.
Wait. The Glenhaven Galleria? Lorne Bisbee, 1979? The pink concrete ziggurat?
That's us! Voted Ontario's ugliest building four years running. The year we lost, we lost to our own parking garage.
Lily, that is the last great example of Pastel Brutalism in North America.
The last? How many were there?
One. Which also makes it the first. And the finest.
What's Pastel Brutalism?
Raw, honest, uncompromising concrete. In the colors of a birthday cake.
Darlene, you cannot knock it down.
Oh, we can, dear. We held a town vote. Ninety-eight percent in favor. The architect voted twice.
Forget the building. Robin, it's your stage. The triumphant return of Robin Sparkles!
Robin Sparkles is dead, Barney. The mall is just finally burying the body.
Besides, nobody remembers that show. It was a Tuesday. Nine people and a pretzel cart.
Kids, it was not nine people and a pretzel cart.
Four hundred of you on a Tuesday, Glenhaven! The fire marshal is weeping! Please welcome Robin Sparkles!
Going up, going up, on the escalator of love! Hold the handrail, baby, it's the safety rule of love!
Thank you, Glenhaven! You are the best mall in the entire province!
And I promise, someday when I'm super old, like thirty, I'll come back and sing for you again!
Pinky swear, Glenhaven!
We'll hold you to that, dear!
Fourteen-year-olds make a lot of promises. I also promised to marry a Zamboni.
She pinky swore a whole mall. Marshall, that's binding.
Legally, no. But in St. Cloud, a pinky swear outranks a notary.
No pressure, dear. You're only our most famous performer.
Well. One of.
One of?
Darlene, has anyone even considered saving the atrium?
Every day, dear. That's why we're knocking it down. Toodle-oo!
I'm going to save that mall.
Ted, the woman who runs it just threw it a going-away party.
And I am getting Robin Sparkles back on that stage.
There is no power on earth that gets me back on that dais.
There was one. It was a bar chart.

scenes.summary: Robin signs off the noon news. Barney and Ted ambush her: Ted has shrunk his campaign to the atrium and his petition has three signatures. Barney has called Darlene forty-one times and has the committee vote: Robin came third, behind Glenny the Beaver and the food court pan flute man, just ahead of the fountain. Robin's pride wins. She's going to Canada.

beats.line: That's Metro News One at noon. Coming up, a Staten Island man who has been mailing his lawn to himself.
Robin, before you say no—
No.
I said before.
Robin! Five minutes of airtime. For the atrium.
Ted, a dead mall in Ontario isn't news. It's Ontario.
I've narrowed the campaign. Forget the whole mall. Just the atrium.
Who told you to aim lower?
The Township of Glenhaven. In writing. Twice.
But we have momentum. Three signatures.
Whose?
Mine. Marshall's. And Marshall's again, in cursive. He felt strongly.
Fine. Don't go. I get it. It's hard to go back when you weren't their first choice.
Excuse me?
I called Darlene forty-one times. On the forty-first, she faxed me the committee vote.
Glenny the Beaver, forty-one. The food court pan flute man, twenty-three. Robin Sparkles, nine. Just ahead of the fountain.
beats.title: Glenhaven's Most Famous Performer: Committee Vote

beats.line: Third? I came third? Behind a beaver and a flute?
A pan flute. Which is technically several flutes, so it's really more of a—
Ted.
The beaver was a sweaty guy in a costume who waved at strollers!
And the strollers loved him.
So why did they invite me?
Glenny's unavailable. Scheduling conflict. And the pan flute man retired to Florida, where pan flutes go to die.
So no, don't go. It's beneath you. Just leave it to the beaver.
Book the limo.
Already booked. Ranjit's been idling outside since Tuesday.
And while you're up there, maybe a few words about the cantilevered—
Ted. I'm not going to Canada to save a building. I'm going to beat a beaver.
Oh, I have so many—
Don't.

scenes.summary: The night before the trip, Barney runs choreography rehearsals. Lily is going for the liquidation sale; Marshall reports the heritage board is just Darlene, who lawyered him. Ted shrinks his crusade to the dais. Robin backs out: she has spent twenty years denying the kid she was. Ted defends the ugly building in terms that are clearly about Robin. A flashback shows Darlene telling a terrified fourteen-year-old to be embarrassing on purpose. Robin decides she owes the kid one show. Then Darlene texts: Ted's structural survey got the demolition moved to seven tomorrow morning. Ranjit is still downstairs.

beats.line: From the top! Five, six, seven, eight, and escalator arms!
Going up. Going up. On the escalator of love.
Robin, you're singing it like the escalator is broken.
It's been twenty years, Barney. The escalator is broken. Please use the stairs.
Okay. Glenhaven liquidation sale. Ninety percent off. Everything must go.
Lilypad, it's a dying mall in Ontario. What could they possibly have?
Marshall, a dying department store is like a beached whale. It feeds the whole village.
Ted. I heard back on your heritage application.
They're designating it?
The Glenhaven Heritage Board is one woman. It's Darlene.
She's also the mall manager, the farewell committee, and the demolition foreman's wife.
I said, that's a conflict of interest. She said, it's a small town, dear. Lawyered.
She lawyered me, Ted. In a cardigan. She didn't even point.
Fine. Forget the atrium. I'll save the dais. One pink dais. That's all I'm asking.
Again! And this time, give me the hair flip.
I'm not going.
What? The beaver wins?
Let the beaver have it.
Robin. What's really going on?
For twenty years, anytime someone says Robin Sparkles, I say, never heard of her. I'm really good at it.
And now I'm supposed to stand on her stage and be her. In front of people who remember.
She's embarrassing, Lily. She wore a scrunchie as a bracelet. On purpose.
Pink concrete. In Ontario. In 1979. The architect knew exactly how that looked. He built it anyway.
Pastel on the outside. Concrete all the way through. People laugh at it because it never learned to be embarrassed.
Are we still talking about the mall?
I'm always talking about the mall.
Dad. Were you talking about the mall?
I was talking about the mall, Penny. Mostly. Largely. Partly the mall.
Five minutes before that show, I tried to run. Darlene found me hiding on a bench by the pretzel cart.
Darlene, what if everybody laughs at me? What if I'm super embarrassing?
Oh, you will be, dear. Everybody's embarrassing at fourteen.
So be embarrassing on purpose. Loud, and in sequins. Then it's called a show.
Okay! I'm gonna be so embarrassing!
Can you hold my retainer?
She knew exactly how it looked. And she went out there anyway. I'm the one who taught her to be ashamed.
She was braver at fourteen than I've been in twenty years. I owe that kid one show.
I'm sorry. I'm just so proud of fourteen-year-old you.
Marshall, you never met her.
I'm meeting her now, Lily!
My survey found the atrium was held up by the paint. They're knocking it down tomorrow. At seven.
beats.title: Darlene

messages.text: Ted dear! Your structural survey came back!
Turns out the atrium was only held up by the paint.
So she comes down tomorrow, 7 a.m. Gala's off. Thanks for caring!

beats.line: Ted. You didn't save the mall. You killed it.
I accelerated its legacy.
Seven a.m.? Glenhaven is nine hours away.
Ranjit's downstairs.
Still? Since Tuesday?
I keep forgetting to tell him he can go home.

scenes.summary: Glenhaven, 7:02 a.m. The mall is already rubble. Ranjit has been in the car since Tuesday. Darlene climbs in with a parting gift for Ted: one pink tile from the center of the dais, and Lily's fountain is on the truck. Ted gives the tile to Robin. Robin keeps her pinky swear in the parking lot with a new verse for the kid she was. Then Darlene reveals she was Glenny the Beaver all along.

beats.line: Glenhaven, Ontario! Seven-oh-two! We made it!
Get ready to see the finest example of Pastel Brutalism in—
Ted. Where's the mall?
That pile. That's the mall.
They said seven. We're a punctual people.
Everything had to go. And it went.
I brought a fog machine. And a backup fog machine.
Hello! Mister Barney, I have now been in this car since Tuesday.
And you've never looked better, buddy.
Thank you. I have started a small garden in the cup holder.
Huh. Twenty years avoiding that stage. The one morning I show up, it's gravel.
I thought I'd be relieved.
You came! I'm so sorry, dear. The boys got excited. There's hockey at ten.
Ted, dear. I saved you something. From the dais.
One pink tile. Darlene, you saved it.
It fell in my purse, dear. Several times.
And Lily, your fountain's on the truck.
You bought the fountain?
Ninety-five percent off, Marshall. It came with the pennies.
Center of the dais. Right where you stood.
Ted, it's a tile.
It's the finest surviving example of Pastel Brutalism in North America.
It's the only surviving example.
Which also makes it the finest.
Darlene. I made Glenhaven a promise.
There's no Glenhaven left, dear. Just the parking lot.
Then the parking lot gets a show.
Fog machine?
No fog machine.
Hey, little Sparkles, sorry I'm late. You were embarrassing. And you were great.
Legendary. I couldn't even wait for it.
Lovely, dear. Truly.
Glenny would've used more arms.
Okay. Who is in the beaver suit? I want a name.
Thirty-one years, dear. Never missed a Saturday.
You're Glenny?
Why do you think I was unavailable? I was hosting.
So I lost to you.
Everybody loses to the beaver, dear.
Kids, the finest surviving example of Pastel Brutalism in North America is the coaster under your Aunt Robin's scotch.
And she never denied being Robin Sparkles again. She only denies coming third.
